changelog/CHANGELOG.html.title: Changelog | Custom Toolbar
changelog/CHANGELOG.html.summary: Changelog 2.0.0 - 2026-08-11 Added Added the explicit module extension API based on IToolbarModule, ILegacyToolbarModule, and ToolbarModuleRegistry. Added Project Settings > NKStudio > Custom Toolbar. Added settings for module visibility, scene search folders, and time scale range and reset values. Added a time scale slider for Unity 2022.3 through Unity 6.2. Added Edit Mode tests for module registration and settings validation. Added compile verification for Unity 2022.3, 6000.0, 6000.3, and 6000.5. Added the extend-custom-toolbar AI skill, which selects the correct module API for the project's Unity version. Changed Moved Unity 6.3 and newer to the official MainToolbar.Refresh lifecycle. Limited reflection on Unity 2022.3 through Unity 6.2 to a single legacy host. Separated FMOD and Localization into optional assemblies. Replaced one-second scene polling with Build Settings and configuration change events. Moved all code into the NKStudio.CustomToolbar namespace. Disabled FMOD Debug, Enter Play Mode, and Scene Switcher consistently during Play Mode. Fixed Prevented duplicate UI and Editor event registration after repeated toolbar reconstruction. Corrected the first-scene button when Build Settings contains no enabled scenes. Corrected duplicate scene names and multiple search-folder handling. Restored the legacy toolbar after Domain Reload configuration and toolbar layout changes. Removed Removed ToolbarExtensionRegistry.LeftToolbarGUI. Removed ToolbarEventHandler. Removed per-feature anonymous playModeStateChanged subscriptions. Removed MainToolbarWindow reflection and generated UI-name lookup on Unity 6.3 and newer. Migration Convert existing ToolbarExtensionRegistry.LeftToolbarGUI extensions to an IToolbarModule implementation registered with ToolbarModuleRegistry.Register(). Move hard-coded scene search paths to Scene Search Folders in Project Settings. 1.0.0 Added Added the Enter Play Mode Options toggle. Added the first Build Settings scene button and scene selection menu. Added the FMOD Debug Overlay toggle. Added the Localization Locale menu. Added the time scale slider for Unity 6. Added Unity 2022 and Unity 6 toolbar support.

manual/ai-skill.html.title: Use the AI skill | Custom Toolbar
manual/ai-skill.html.summary: Use the AI skill Custom Toolbar includes an extend-custom-toolbar skill for AI coding agents. The skill guides the agent through Unity version selection, file placement, assembly references, module implementation, and validation. Skill location The skill is included in the installed package at: Packages/com.nkstudio.custom-toolbar/Skills/extend-custom-toolbar/SKILL.md The complete extend-custom-toolbar folder contains the main instructions and separate implementation references for supported Unity versions. What the skill does The skill instructs the agent to: read ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt as the source of truth for the Unity Editor version; use IToolbarModule and ILegacyToolbarModule on Unity 2022.3 through 6000.2; use Unity's official MainToolbarElement API on Unity 6000.3 or newer; create project-specific modules under Assets/Editor/ToolbarModules instead of editing the installed package; add an Editor-only assembly reference when required; check module IDs, refresh paths, lifecycle subscriptions, and compilation. Ask an agent to use the skill Provide the skill path explicitly in your request: Read Packages/com.nkstudio.custom-toolbar/Skills/extend-custom-toolbar/SKILL.md and add a new Custom Toolbar module to this project. Include the desired control type, toolbar position, action, and Play Mode behavior in the request when known. Automatic skill discovery If the coding agent supports automatic skill discovery, install or copy the entire extend-custom-toolbar folder into that agent's skills directory. Keep the referenced files together with SKILL.md; the skill selects one of them after checking the project's Unity version. For the underlying module APIs and manual examples, see Create a custom module.

manual/custom-modules.html.title: Create a custom module | Custom Toolbar
manual/custom-modules.html.summary: Create a custom module You can develop custom toolbar modules tailored to your project environment by implementing the IToolbarModule interface. Toolbar scripts should be created under an Editor folder. Choose the API for your Unity version Read ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt and use the implementation that matches m_EditorVersion. Unity version Module implementation 6000.3 or newer Implement IToolbarModule. Declare UI with Unity's official MainToolbarElement API. 2022.3 through 6000.2 Implement IToolbarModule and ILegacyToolbarModule. Add UI through LegacyToolbarBuilder. Custom Toolbar does not support Unity versions earlier than 2022.3. Register the module Module registration works the same way across all supported Unity versions. Every module needs a stable, globally unique ID and must register exactly once from an [InitializeOnLoad] static constructor. using NKStudio.CustomToolbar; using UnityEditor; [InitializeOnLoad] internal sealed class ExampleToolbarModule : IToolbarModule { private const string ModuleId = "Company.Product.Toolbar.Example"; static ExampleToolbarModule() { ToolbarModuleRegistry.Register(new ExampleToolbarModule()); } public string Id => ModuleId; public void Refresh(ToolbarRefreshReason reason) { // Refresh this module's toolbar state. } } Do not subscribe separately to EditorApplication.playModeStateChanged or EditorBuildSettings.sceneListChanged. The toolbar host sends the corresponding ToolbarRefreshReason to registered modules. Unity 6000.3 or newer Use Unity's public Main Toolbar API. The path passed to MainToolbar.Refresh must exactly match the path declared by MainToolbarElement. using NKStudio.CustomToolbar; using UnityEditor; using UnityEditor.Toolbars; [InitializeOnLoad] internal sealed class ModernExampleToolbarModule : IToolbarModule { private const string ModuleId = "Company.Product.Toolbar.Example"; private const string ElementPath = "Company Toolbar/Example"; static ModernExampleToolbarModule() { ToolbarModuleRegistry.Register(new ModernExampleToolbarModule()); } public string Id => ModuleId; public void Refresh(ToolbarRefreshReason reason) { if (reason is ToolbarRefreshReason.Initialized or ToolbarRefreshReason.PlayModeChanged) MainToolbar.Refresh(ElementPath); } [MainToolbarElement( ElementPath, defaultDockPosition = MainToolbarDockPosition.Right, defaultDockIndex = 20)] private static MainToolbarElement CreateElement() { var content = new MainToolbarContent("Example", "Run an Editor action."); return new MainToolbarButton(content, OnClick) { enabled = ToolbarAvailability.InEditMode }; } private static void OnClick() { // Run an Editor-only action. } } Unity 2022.3 through 6000.2 compatibility For earlier supported versions, implement ILegacyToolbarModule and create UI Toolkit controls in BuildLegacy. The package owns all toolbar reflection. using NKStudio.CustomToolbar; using UnityEditor; using UnityEditor.UIElements; [InitializeOnLoad] internal sealed class LegacyExampleToolbarModule : IToolbarModule, ILegacyToolbarModule { private const string ModuleId = "Company.Product.Toolbar.Example"; private ToolbarButton _button; static LegacyExampleToolbarModule() { ToolbarModuleRegistry.Register(new LegacyExampleToolbarModule()); } public string Id => ModuleId; public void Refresh(ToolbarRefreshReason reason) { _button?.SetEnabled(ToolbarAvailability.InEditMode); } public void BuildLegacy(LegacyToolbarBuilder builder) { _button = new ToolbarButton(OnClick) { text = "Example" }; _button.SetEnabled(ToolbarAvailability.InEditMode); builder.Add(LegacyToolbarZone.Right, _button); } private static void OnClick() { // Run an Editor-only action. } } Add every element through LegacyToolbarBuilder.Add. Available zones are Left, CenterLeft, CenterRight, and Right. Validation checklist Confirm the module ID is not duplicated in Assets or Packages. Keep the action Editor-only and use ToolbarAvailability.InEditMode for controls that must be disabled in Play Mode. For Unity 6000.3 or newer, use the exact same element path for the attribute and refresh call. For earlier supported versions, add every element through LegacyToolbarBuilder. Compile and test with the Unity version recorded in ProjectVersion.txt. Choose the enabled state of a toolbar element ToolbarAvailability provides four properties for the enabled value of a toolbar element. Choose the property whose name matches the intended behavior instead of interpreting a negated condition. Property When the element is enabled Use case InEditMode In Edit Mode Editor actions that must not run in Play Mode or while entering Play Mode InPlayMode During actual Play Mode Actions available only while the game is running Always Always Actions available regardless of the Editor state Never Never Visible actions that are not currently available On Unity 6000.3 or newer, assign the desired property to enabled in the element factory. The following button is enabled only in Edit Mode. [MainToolbarElement( ElementPath, defaultDockPosition = MainToolbarDockPosition.Right, defaultDockIndex = 20)] private static MainToolbarElement CreateElement() { var content = new MainToolbarContent("Example", "Run an Editor action."); return new MainToolbarButton(content, OnClick) { enabled = ToolbarAvailability.InEditMode }; } When using InEditMode or InPlayMode, recreate the element during initialization and whenever the Play Mode state changes. public void Refresh(ToolbarRefreshReason reason) { if (reason is ToolbarRefreshReason.Initialized or ToolbarRefreshReason.PlayModeChanged) MainToolbar.Refresh(ElementPath); } Tip ModernToolbarHost sends ToolbarRefreshReason.PlayModeChanged to every registered module whenever the Play Mode state changes. If the module is registered with ToolbarModuleRegistry, its state updates without a separate EditorApplication.playModeStateChanged subscription. Always and Never do not change with Play Mode, so they do not require recreation for state changes. Display a dynamic value in a label To display an external value in a toolbar label, as the Scene Switcher does, read the value inside CreateElement(). The first argument of the MainToolbarContent constructor is the label shown in the toolbar. private static MainToolbarElement CreateElement() { string label = MyToolbarData.CurrentLabel; var content = new MainToolbarContent( label, "Display the current value."); return new MainToolbarButton(content, OnClick) { enabled = ToolbarAvailability.InEditMode }; } The asset's built-in Scene Switcher displays the name of the first enabled scene in Build Settings. Its core structure is as follows. public void Refresh(ToolbarRefreshReason reason) { if (reason is ToolbarRefreshReason.Initialized or ToolbarRefreshReason.SceneListChanged) { MainToolbar.Refresh(ElementPath); } } [MainToolbarElement(ElementPath)] private static MainToolbarElement CreateElement() { string label = $"Start '{SceneHelper.FirstSceneName}'"; return new MainToolbarButton( new MainToolbarContent(label, "Start the first scene in Build Settings."), SceneHelper.MoveFirstScene) { enabled = ToolbarAvailability.InEditMode && SceneHelper.HasFirstScene }; } Important A label does not change automatically when its source value changes. CreateElement() uses the value available when the element is created, so call MainToolbar.Refresh(ElementPath) in response to the source value's change event to apply the new label. SceneHelper is the class that retrieves and formats values for the asset's built-in Scene Switcher. Follow the same pattern in a custom module: keep data handling in a separate Helper or Provider class, and let the toolbar class focus on presenting that value.

manual/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | Custom Toolbar
manual/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started Custom Toolbar registers its available modules after Unity imports the package. No component needs to be added to a scene. Configure scene folders Open Edit > Project Settings > NKStudio > Custom Toolbar. Expand Scene Search Folders. Add Assets or one or more folders under it, such as Assets/Scenes. The scene menu lists scenes found in those folders. Invalid folders, duplicate paths, and paths outside Assets are removed when the setting is saved. The first-scene button opens the first enabled scene in File > Build Profiles (called Build Settings in earlier Unity versions). Choose visible modules Use Visible Modules in the same settings page to show or hide each feature: Enter Play Mode Options Scene Switcher Time Scale Localization FMOD Debug Localization and FMOD Debug also require their optional packages. Changing a visibility setting refreshes the toolbar. Configure time scale Set the minimum, maximum, and reset values under Time Scale. The reset value is kept within the configured minimum and maximum range. Use the toolbar slider to change Time.timeScale. Open its menu to restore the configured reset value.

manual/index.html.title: Custom Toolbar | Custom Toolbar
manual/index.html.summary: Custom Toolbar Custom Toolbar is a modular Editor extension that puts frequently used project controls on Unity's main toolbar. Features Toggle Enter Play Mode Options without opening Project Settings. Open the first enabled scene in Build Settings. Select a scene from configured project folders. Adjust and reset Time.timeScale. Toggle the FMOD Debug Overlay when FMOD for Unity is installed. Select the active locale when Unity Localization is installed. Custom Toolbar supports Unity 2022.3 LTS through Unity 6. Unity 6.3 and newer use the official Main Toolbar API; earlier supported versions use the package's legacy toolbar host. Start with Requirements, then follow Installation and Getting started. To add a project-specific control, see Create a custom module.

manual/installation.html.title: Installation | Custom Toolbar
manual/installation.html.summary: Installation Package installation Install Custom Toolbar from its Git repository URL with Unity Package Manager. Make sure Git is installed. Open the Package Manager. Click the + button and select Install package from git URL.... Enter the package repository URL, then click Install. https://github.com/NK-Studio/com.nkstudio.custom-toolbar.git

manual/project-settings.html.title: Project settings | Custom Toolbar
manual/project-settings.html.summary: Project settings Open Edit > Project Settings > NKStudio > Custom Toolbar. Settings are stored per project in ProjectSettings/CustomToolbarSettings.asset. Setting Purpose Default Show Enter Play Mode Shows the Enter Play Mode Options toggle. On Show Scene Switcher Shows the first-scene button and scene menu. On Show Time Scale Shows the time scale control. On Show Localization Shows the optional Localization menu. On Show FMOD Debug Shows the optional FMOD Debug toggle. On Scene Search Folders Selects the Assets folders searched by the scene menu. Assets/Scenes Minimum Time Scale Sets the slider's minimum value. 0 Maximum Time Scale Sets the slider's maximum value. 5 Reset Time Scale Sets the value used by the reset action. 1 Scene folder paths are normalized when saved. The maximum time scale cannot be lower than the minimum, and the reset value is clamped to that range.

manual/requirements.html.title: Requirements | Custom Toolbar
manual/requirements.html.summary: Requirements Unity version Custom Toolbar 2.0.0 requires Unity 2022.3 or newer. The package is Editor-only and does not add runtime components to your build. Optional integrations The core toolbar has no dependency on FMOD or Unity Localization. Their toolbar modules compile only when the matching package is installed. Module Optional package Supported version FMOD Debug FMOD for Unity (com.firelight.fmod-for-unity) 2.2.0 or newer, below 3.0.0 Localization Unity Localization (com.unity.localization) 1.0.0 or newer, below 2.0.0 All other modules are available immediately after installing Custom Toolbar.

manual/toolbar-controls.html.title: Toolbar controls | Custom Toolbar
manual/toolbar-controls.html.summary: Toolbar controls Enter Play Mode Options The toggle enables or disables Unity's Enter Play Mode Options. It is disabled while the Editor is in Play Mode. Scene Switcher The Start Scene button on the left instantly opens the first enabled scene in the project's Build Settings or Build Profiles. The Scene Selection menu on the right allows you to quickly browse and switch between scenes located in the folders configured under Scene Search Folders. Both controls are disabled in Play Mode. When switching scenes, Unity will automatically prompt you to save any unsaved changes if necessary. Time Scale The slider changes Time.timeScale in Edit Mode or Play Mode. Its reset action restores the value configured in Project Settings. FMOD Debug When FMOD for Unity is installed, the toggle controls the FMOD Debug Overlay. The control is disabled in Play Mode. Localization When Unity Localization is installed, the menu selects the active locale. It remains available in Edit Mode and Play Mode.
